office_does: Okanogan County's three commissioners set the county budget and property tax levy, pass ordinances and run county government; candidates are nominated by district and elected countywide.
race_blurb: Two Republicans. Incumbent Jon Neal, a former Oroville mayor, voted with the board to send a levy lid lift to the August ballot and accepted cuts when it failed; Farm Bureau leader Trinity Hightower Stucker, endorsed by the county Republican Party, opposed the lid lift and proposes cuts first, including commissioner pay. Stucker led the District 3 primary 51% to 48%.

candidates.summary: Okanogan County Commissioner for District 3 since 2023, former Oroville mayor and council member, and 34-year owner of an Oroville auto body shop.
highlights: Voted 'reluctantly' with the full board to put the levy lid lift on the August ballot, then said 'I honestly am not in support of the levy lid lift either' [S2][S5]
After its defeat: 'time for some cuts, I guess. The people have spoken' [S4]
Pledges to 'fight Olympia against state government overreach regarding excessive taxation and over regulation' [S1]
Puts state unfunded mandates at about $3.5 million a year for the county [S3][S5]

experience.basis: Incumbent commissioner since the 2022 election, with prior service as Oroville mayor and council member.

taxes.basis: Opposes state taxation and lobbied against the millionaire's tax, but voted to send the county levy lid lift to voters while saying he did not personally support it.

candidates.summary: Tonasket farm owner, Washington State Farm Bureau board director and former state Senate session aide, running for her first county office with the county Republican Party's endorsement.
highlights: Opposed the 2026 levy lid lift as 'a Band-Aid': 'My plan is for that levy to fail' [S5][S6]
Backs a volunteer review's more than $3 million in proposed cuts, including 10% pay cuts for commissioners and department heads [S5][S6]
Platform: lower taxes, efficiency audits, faster permitting and year-round wildfire fuel reduction [S1][S3]
Endorsed by the Okanogan County Republican Party [S7]

taxes.basis: Campaigns on 'lower taxes' and worked for the county's levy lid lift to fail.

spending.basis: Proposes more than $3 million in cuts, 10% pay cuts for commissioners and department heads, and efficiency audits before new revenue.

experience.basis: First run for county office, challenging the incumbent; brings Farm Bureau and legislative-aide experience rather than an elected record.

reform.basis: Calls for transparent government and efficiency audits, saying residents feel they are 'paying more and getting less'.
